---
title: "How do I...?"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

Short answers to common tasks.  Each recipe is a few lines of code with
a link to the page that explains it in full.

All recipes use this one-compartment oral model with between-subject
variability and proportional residual error:

```{r setup}
library(rxode2)

mod <- function() {
  ini({
    tka <- log(1.15)
    tcl <- log(0.135)
    tv <- log(8)
    eta.ka ~ 0.6
    eta.cl ~ 0.3
    eta.v ~ 0.1
    prop.sd <- 0.1
  })
  model({
    ka <- exp(tka + eta.ka)
    cl <- exp(tcl + eta.cl)
    v <- exp(tv + eta.v)
    d/dt(depot) <- -ka * depot
    d/dt(center) <- ka * depot - cl / v * center
    cp <- center / v
    cp ~ prop(prop.sd)
  })
}
```

## Dosing

### ...give a dose every 12 hours for a week?

```{r}
ev <- et(amt = 300, ii = 12, until = 168) |>
  et(seq(0, 168, by = 1))
s <- rxSolve(mod, ev)
plot(s, cp)
```

More: [Building event tables with et()](rxode2-event-table.html).

### ...give a loading dose followed by maintenance doses?

```{r}
ev <- et(amt = 600) |>
  et(time = 12, amt = 300, ii = 12, until = 168) |>
  et(seq(0, 168, by = 1))
```

More: [Combining event tables](rxode2-event-table-combine.html).

### ...give an infusion?

Give the duration with `dur` (or the rate with `rate`), dosing into the
central compartment:

```{r}
ev <- et(amt = 300, dur = 2, cmt = "center") |>
  et(seq(0, 24, by = 0.5))
```

More: [Dosing event types](rxode2-event-types.html#infusion-doses).

### ...start at steady state?

```{r}
ev <- et(amt = 300, ii = 12, ss = 1) |>
  et(seq(0, 24, by = 0.5))
```

More: [Dosing event types](rxode2-event-types.html#steady-state).

### ...use my own NONMEM-style dataset?

Pass the data frame straight to `rxSolve()`; columns are matched by
name (`ID`, `TIME`, `AMT`, `EVID`, `CMT`, ...):

```{r}
d <- data.frame(ID = 1, TIME = c(0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12),
                AMT = c(300, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0), EVID = c(1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
                CMT = c("depot", rep("center", 5)))
s <- rxSolve(mod, d)
```

More: [Dataset columns](rxode2-dataset-columns.html).

### ...dose based on the current model state?

Use `bolus()`, `infuse()` and friends inside `model()`.

More: [Dosing from inside the model](adaptive-dosing.html).

## Simulation

### ...simulate the typical individual (no variability)?

```{r}
ev <- et(amt = 300, ii = 12, until = 72) |>
  et(seq(0, 72, by = 0.5))
s <- rxSolve(zeroRe(mod), ev)
```

More: `?zeroRe`.

### ...simulate a population?

```{r}
s <- rxSolve(mod, ev, nSub = 100)
```

Each subject draws its own `eta` values from the `ini()` block.  More:
[Simulating populations](rxode2-sim-var.html).

### ...get simulated observations with residual error?

The endpoint `cp ~ prop(prop.sd)` adds residual error; the simulated
observation is in the `sim` column, the prediction stays in `cp`
(subjects simulated with `nSub` are numbered in `sim.id`):

```{r}
head(s[, c("sim.id", "time", "cp", "sim")])
```

### ...make a simulation reproducible?

```{r}
s1 <- rxSolve(mod, ev, nSub = 10, seed = 42)
s2 <- rxSolve(mod, ev, nSub = 10, seed = 42)
all.equal(s1$sim, s2$sim)
```

More: `?rxWithSeed`.

### ...add parameter uncertainty?

Give a covariance matrix for the population parameters with `thetaMat`
and the number of studies with `nStud`:

```{r}
s <- rxSolve(mod, ev, nSub = 20, nStud = 5,
             thetaMat = lotri::lotri(tcl ~ 0.01, tv ~ 0.01))
```

More: [Parameter uncertainty](rxode2-parameter-uncertainty.html).

### ...summarize a simulation with prediction intervals?

```{r}
s <- rxSolve(mod, ev, nSub = 200, seed = 42)
ci <- confint(s, "sim", level = 0.90)
plot(ci)
```

More: [Summarizing simulations with confint()](rxode2-confint.html).

### ...simulate between-occasion variability?

More: [Nesting levels](rxode2-nesting.html).

## Covariates

### ...add a covariate effect?

Pipe a new line into the model; the covariate `WT` becomes an input:

```{r}
modWt <- mod |>
  model(cl <- exp(tcl + eta.cl) * (WT / 70)^0.75)
```

More: [Modifying models](Modifying-Models.html).

### ...give each subject their own covariate value?

```{r}
s <- rxSolve(modWt, ev,
             iCov = data.frame(id = 1:4, WT = c(50, 70, 90, 110)))
```

More: [Covariates](rxode2-covariates.html).

### ...use a covariate that changes over time?

Add it as a column of the data; values are interpolated between rows:

```{r}
d <- as.data.frame(et(amt = 300, ii = 24, until = 96) |>
                     et(seq(0, 96, by = 4)))
d$WT <- 70 - d$time / 24
s <- rxSolve(modWt, d)
```

More: [Covariates](rxode2-covariates.html).

## Output and speed

### ...get output only at specific times?

```{r}
ev <- et(amt = 300) |> et(c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24))
rxSolve(zeroRe(mod), ev)
```

### ...keep input columns in the output?

```{r}
d$GROUP <- "A"
s <- rxSolve(modWt, d, keep = c("WT", "GROUP"))
head(s[, c("time", "cp", "WT", "GROUP")])
```

### ...plot the result?

```{r}
plot(s, cp)
```

More: [Plotting](rxode2-plot.html).

### ...solve faster?

Use more threads for multi-subject problems:

```{r}
s <- rxSolve(mod, ev, nSub = 100, cores = 2)
```

More: [Speeding up solving](rxode2-speed.html).

### ...solve a population too large for memory?

More: [Out-of-memory solving](rxode2-oom-solve.html).

## Models

### ...change an initial estimate or fix a parameter?

```{r}
mod2 <- mod |> ini(tcl = log(0.2))
mod3 <- mod |> ini(tv = fix)
```

More: [Modifying models](Modifying-Models.html).

### ...see one line of a model?

```{r}
modelExtract(mod, cl)
```

### ...use a low-level `rxode2()` model or classic event table?

More: [Low-level models and other input styles](rxode2-classic-models.html).
